newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline says current stg would cut 97 pfts.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says current stg would cut 97 pfts.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Tuesday that if sterling continued at its current realtively high levels for the rest of the year, its pre-tax profits would be cut by arond 5 percent.

In a telephone interview with Reuters after publication of full-year results, finance director Hugh Collum said "it is a difficult story to be relaiable on, but we are saying that if exchange rates stay where they are there could be a five percent impact" on pre-tax profits.

Collum said the company hoped to reach a settlement with the U.S. government in its dispute over the charging practices of the Clinical Laboratories diagnostic division "shortly," possibly within the next two months.

He said he was happy that the 250 million stg provision for a settlement of the dispute, which centres on allegations that Clinical Laboratories overcharged the federally-funded Medicare programme, were "adequate."

The finance director also told Reuters that capital expenditure at the group in 1997 would be around 550 million stg. Collum also told Reuters that the Diversified Pharmaceutical Services (DPS) pharmacy benefit management business, which saw the number of lives covered rise by 27 percent last year to 33 million, was unlikely to expand its coverage at the same pace in 1997.

"We'd hope to see it increase, but there is no expectation of it rising at the same rate," Collum said, adding that DPS, which was acquired in 1994, is "really on the border line" of being profitable.
